newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends below 6,000 level, extends losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends below 6,000 level, extends losing streak.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks extended their losing streak to a fourth session Thursday as the Dow Jones industrial average ended below 6,000 for the first time in two weeks amid stepped-up profit-taking.
The Dow fell 43.98 points to 5,992.48 after sliding 58 points over the first three days of the week. It was the first close below 6,000 since Oct. 10 for the index of 30 blue-chip stocks.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,203 to 1,112 on heavy volume of 415 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We started a correction on Monday and we're still in it," said Alfred Goldman, technical research director of A.G. Edwards. "It's a backing-and-filling affair that might wear people out for a week or two."
He said the profit-taking was in the shares of oil, household products and food companies that had been strong recently.
The Dow rode a wild rollercoaster in the afternoon, losing nearly 50 points before bouncing back and then retreating at the close.
The shares of big oil companies fell as crude oil prices sank after soaring to a post-Gulf War high of more than $26 a barrel on supply worries.
Texaco slumped 2-7/8 to 100-3/4, Exxon was off 1-3/8 to 87-1/4 and Chevron lost 3/4 to 66-1/2.
Crude oil closed 35 cents lower at $24.51 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Procter & Gamble lost 2-1/4 to 94 after the consumer products giant reported record quarter earnings but a drop in worldwide sales due to the strong dollar.
A.G. Edwards' Goldman said the market was taking a "normal pause to refresh" after jumping 18 percent since July and 10 percent since Labour Day at the start of September.
"People are itchy to take profits," said Robert Stovall, president of Stovall/Twenty-First. "It's easy to rationalise. It's a choppy, marking time day."
Meanwhile, the Treasury bond market fell on news that weekly jobless claims fell more than expected to 320,000 for the week ended Oct. 19, indicating that the nation's labour market remains tight.
The benchmark 30-year bond was down a quarter point, raising its yield to 6.85 percent from 6.83 percent on Wednesday.
Wall Street is awaiting Friday's release of September durable goods. Economists are predicting a 2.0 percent increase.
Among individual shares, United Technologies surged 4-1/8 to 127-5/8. The company on Wednesday reported a jump in quarterly profits and forecast earnings will grow by 15 percent next year.
Lucent rose 1-5/8 to 50 after reporting strong profits for the latest quarter.
AMP Inc. slumped 3-1/4 to 35. It posted a drop in earnings and warned of "significant price erosion" in personal computers and communications.

Shares of computer disk drive manufacturers were stronger after Read-Rite and Western Digital reported healthy quarters. Read-Rite gained 1/2 to 17-7/8, Western Digital rose 2-3/4 to 48-1/4 and Seagate Technology added 2-3/8 to 65-7/8.
Electronic Arts climbed 4-1/8 to 37-1/2 after reporting a near doubling in quarterly results.
James River surged 3-1/2 to 31-5/8 also on upbeat profits.
Alcoa added 1-7/8 to 59-7/8. Morgan Stanley upgraded its opinion of the aluminum producer.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 0.88 of a point to 1,227.00.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 4.98 to 702.29. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.93 to 569.80.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 2.13 to 373.78. The average share was down 23 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,844.034 down 36.560 or 0.53 percent.
